plannerAnswers.question: What did you like most about this prompt?
plannerAnswers.answer: The mix of hard, checkable requirements (10% music, a 10-second attract mode, one HTML file, a Hub harness that passes or fails) with real freedom on genre, camera and effort. The 'This computer' section was the best part: because it gave me working browsers, tools and stand-ins, I could run the engine and the Hub harness before writing a word, so the plan could state what works instead of what the docs imply.

plannerAnswers.question: What was confusing?
plannerAnswers.answer: Four things. First, the browser flags: the WebGPU flags listed in TASK.md do not run this engine here. The device is lost and the picture stays blank until --use-angle=swiftshader is added, which is what the kit's own check.mjs uses. Second, 'Follow the hub docs for multiplayer as well as for the game on its own': the protocol only says a game must keep working outside a session, so I could not tell whether multiplayer outside the Hub is required. I planned it anyway, with a Visit mode. Third, the title must be a riff on the source's name while the game must be original, with no guidance on how close a riff may sit, so I told builders the pun must work by itself. Fourth, TASK.md is written for the builder, so I had to decide how much of the builder-only material (Source Information, feedback questions, exit interview) belonged in a plan that must leave those file names out; I covered it by reference.

plannerAnswers.question: What was the hardest thing to do?
plannerAnswers.answer: Setting scope for a reader I cannot talk to. The source is huge, and the brief wants all of its feel, no stubs and a complete demo, yet I do not know the builders' budget. I compressed the year to 16 days, wrote content counts as floor and target, ordered the build, and said what may never be cut. A close second was capturing what makes the source distinctive without recreating it: the mechanics stay, but every name, character, species-for-role pairing, melody and layout had to be new, and the replacements still had to be funny.

plannerAnswers.question: What would you change in this prompt?
plannerAnswers.answer: Correct the WebGPU flags in 'This computer', or point to the set in the kit's check.mjs; as written, a builder's first browser run shows a blank screen. Note that python3 -m http.server prints its port only when unbuffered, so a script reading it through a pipe needs -u. State plainly whether multiplayer outside the Hub is required, and the minimum if so. Tell the planner the builders' model, effort and rough time budget, and how many hours 'long enough to show ALL features' should mean, since scope depends on all of these. Say outright that a planner may prototype in a scratch folder, because that is where the most useful findings came from. Finally, mark which TASK.md sections are for the builder only, so the planner knows what the plan must carry and what it can leave to them.
